skill.name: enact-text-summarizer
skill.description: Analyzes supplied text and returns word, character, sentence, average word length, and reading time statistics.
skill.summary: Measure text length, sentence count, average word length, and estimated reading time.
skill.author: EnactProtocol

security_audit.summary: The four static external-command findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and a JavaScript template literal. Semantic review found raw user input interpolation in the Enact command string, which may allow shell command injection. The author should fix command argument handling before publication.

remediation.issue: Raw user text is interpolated into the command string.
remediation.suggestion: Pass text through a safely escaped argument, stdin, or runner-managed JSON input. Avoid placing ${text} directly inside a shell command string.

finding_verdicts.reason: This is an opening Markdown bash code fence for documentation, not executable skill code. The sample command does not run during skill execution.
This is a Markdown fence terminator followed by prose feature text. It is documentation content, not Ruby or shell backtick execution.
This is an opening Markdown JSON code fence for an example output block. It is not executed by the skill runtime.
The backticks are a JavaScript template literal used to format an error string. No shell command is executed at this location.

semantic_findings.title: User Input Interpolated Into Command String
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md inserts user-controlled text into the command string without quoting or argument escaping. This can permit shell command injection if the runner uses shell parsing.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command template includes raw ${text}, and text is required user input. The exact runner execution model is not shown, so confidence is high but not absolute.

content.value_statement: Writers and teams need quick size and readability signals for plain text. This skill returns counts and reading-time estimates from a single text input.
actual_capabilities: Estimates sentence count from periods, exclamation marks, and question marks.
Calculates average word length to two decimal places.
Estimates reading time at 200 words per minute.
limitations: It does not create semantic summaries or rewrite text.
Sentence counts are heuristic and can misread abbreviations or unusual punctuation.
Very long text may hit command length limits in some runners.
It does not detect tone, topic, sentiment, or factual accuracy.

use_cases.title: Check Draft Length
use_cases.description: Measure word count, sentence count, and reading time before publishing short articles.

use_cases.title: Review Support Messages
use_cases.description: Measure response length so customer messages stay concise and easy to scan.

use_cases.title: Prepare Learning Material
use_cases.description: Estimate reading time for assignments, lesson text, and short study materials.

prompt_templates.title: Quick Text Metrics
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner check for one pasted passage.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use enact-text-summarizer to analyze this text: [paste text]. Return the key counts and reading time.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Draft Length
prompt_templates.scenario: Check one draft against a target length.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the pasted draft with enact-text-summarizer. Tell me whether it fits a target of [target words] and [target minutes].

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Editorial Notes
prompt_templates.scenario: Use metrics to guide a writing review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run enact-text-summarizer on this article excerpt. Use the results to suggest where the draft may need shorter sections.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Message Variants
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced comparison across several text options.
prompt_templates.prompt: For each message variant, run enact-text-summarizer separately. Compare word count, sentence count, average word length, and reading time.

output_examples.input: A short feature announcement paragraph for a product release.
output_examples.output: The result reports word count, non-space character count, estimated sentences, average word length, and reading time.

output_examples.input: A customer support reply that needs a quick length check.
output_examples.output: The result shows whether the reply is concise by reporting counts and an estimated reading time.

best_practices: Use plain text input when you need counts instead of semantic summaries.
Review sentence estimates manually when text contains abbreviations or bullet lists.
Avoid sensitive text in command-line workflows unless process arguments are protected.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill as a factual summarizer.
Do not rely on sentence counts for legal or compliance limits without review.
Do not pass untrusted shell fragments as text until command escaping is fixed.

faq.question: Does this skill write files?
faq.answer: No. The script reads one text argument and prints analysis results.

faq.question: Does it summarize meaning?
faq.answer: No. It measures text statistics and reading time. It does not create an abstract.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: It is marked compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: How is reading time calculated?
faq.answer: It divides the word count by 200 words per minute.

faq.question: Can it process long documents?
faq.answer: It can process text passed as one argument, but very long content may hit command length limits.

faq.question: Does it work for all languages?
faq.answer: It works best for whitespace-separated text. Accuracy is lower for languages without spaces.
